page: Microsoft Azure D96as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 96 vCPUs sourced from 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at up to 3.7 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. Memory capacity totals 384.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware vector support includes AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16 instruction sets alongside standard cryptographic extensions like AES and SHA-NI.

Benchmark testing demonstrates high compute capabilities. In stress-ng testing, the instance achieved a multi-core score of 147,439.18, ranking in the top 10% tier of multi-threaded compute performance. Single-core stress-ng performance reached 3,077.43, placing it within the top 25%. In in-memory data store tests, the machine sustained 104.36 million operations per second during Redis SET operations, placing in the top 25% bracket for caching workload throughput.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware accelerators such as GPUs, relying on remote persistent disks for data storage. As a diskless VM configuration, it provides cost efficiency by avoiding charges for unused ephemeral disks while delivering dedicated, high-density CPU and memory capacity. Primary workloads include enterprise web applications, large relational and NoSQL databases, memory caching layers, continuous integration pipelines, and distributed data processing tasks requiring high core counts.
description: Microsoft Azure D96as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by a 48-core, 96-thread AMD EPYC 9V74 processor reaching frequencies up to 3.7 GHz. Configured with an x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance pairs its 96 vCPUs with 384.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Compute benchmarks confirm high performance, highlighted by a multi-core stress-ng score in the top 10% tier and single-core output in the top 25%. In-memory throughput is also high, delivering 104.36 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance provides no bundled local NVMe storage and contains zero GPUs, focusing hardware resources exclusively on compute and system memory. This resource profile suits large-scale application backends, extensive database servers, in-memory caching platforms, and parallel batch processing jobs that utilize remote network-attached volumes.
